admin.flag.unverifiedHelp: The facts of this item could not be checked against a public source. It can be stored, but never approved.
admin.queue.title: Validation queue
admin.queue.lead: Everything waiting for a decision. Only an approved item ever reaches the visitor app.
admin.queue.villagesUnavailable: The village list could not be loaded; village names are shown as the keys the API sent.
admin.queue.caption: Items waiting for validation
admin.queue.footnote: Sample data. Approving an item publishes it to the visitor app; rejecting returns it to the author with a note.
admin.item.hostConfirmed: Fields the host entered and confirmed
admin.item.hostConfirmedHelp: Price, season, capacity and accessibility are always entered and confirmed by the host. The model never fills them in.
admin.item.consentMissing: no consent record — this listing cannot be approved
admin.item.consentUnknown: the API did not report a consent record
admin.item.remainingFields: Other fields returned by the API
admin.item.fieldsLead: Every field as the API returned it, with the two languages side by side.
admin.item.provenanceLead: Who did what, when, to which version, and on which source.
admin.field.title: Title
admin.field.name: Name
admin.provenance.empty: No provenance has been recorded for this item yet.
admin.transition.gateCallout: Approving publishes the item to the visitor app. Nothing reaches visitors without this step.
admin.transition.unverifiedCallout: An item whose facts are marked unverified can never be approved, and a listing can never be approved without a consent record.
admin.transition.blockedByFacts: The facts of this item are marked unverified, so approval will be refused (409). Check them against a public source and record the source first.
admin.transition.noteHelp: The note is stored in the provenance trail and in the audit log. Rejecting requires one.
admin.transition.noteRequired: A note is required when rejecting.
admin.transition.none: A {role} cannot move an item out of the status {status}.
admin.audit.title: Audit log
admin.audit.lead: Every write, with its actor and its resource. The detail column never carries personal data.
admin.audit.validatorOnly: The audit log is available to validators only.
admin.audit.caption: Entries of the audit log
admin.audit.footnote: Entries are written by the backend and cannot be edited from this screen.
admin.new.title: New heritage entry
admin.new.lead: The entry is always saved as a draft: nothing skips the validation gate.
admin.new.bothLanguages: Write both languages. A published field is never machine-translated without saying so.
admin.new.sourceHelp: Say where the facts come from: a publication, an archive, or the person who told them.
admin.new.factsVerified: The facts were checked against a public source
admin.new.factsVerifiedHelp: Leave this unchecked when you could not check them. An unverified entry can be saved, but never approved.
admin.new.draftNote: The entry enters the queue as a draft and waits for a validator.
admin.login.title: Sign in
admin.login.lead: One gate for all four roles of the prototype.
admin.login.name: Name
admin.login.sampleLead: Fictional people, one per role. The password is {password} and is not a secret.
admin.login.sampleNote: No real person and no real provider appears anywhere in this prototype.
admin.login.roleHelp.host: Hosts record their offer by voice, confirm the extracted listing and give consent before it is validated.
admin.login.roleHelp.ambassador: Ambassadors help hosts, write heritage entries and pre-review drafts.
admin.login.roleHelp.validator: Validators approve or reject content, and they read the audit log.
admin.login.roleHelp.institution: Institutions read the published KPI run and the disclosure review behind it.
admin.kpi.caption: K01–K23 of the published run. A cell backed by fewer than {k} people or devices is never shown as a number.
admin.kpi.reasonPrimary: fewer than {k} distinct people or devices behind the cell
admin.kpi.reasonSecondary: hidden so that the suppressed cell cannot be recovered from the total
admin.kpi.reason.secondary: hidden so that the suppressed cell cannot be recovered from the total
admin.kpi.reason.small_cell: a date × activity × gender cell below the threshold; it is not even stored
admin.kpi.reason.unsupported spec: the definition of this indicator cannot be computed yet
admin.kpi.noBreakdown: this run has no breakdown rows
admin.kpi.legendPrimary: Primary suppression: a cell backed by fewer than {k} distinct people or devices shows “suppressed (k<{k})” and never a number.
admin.kpi.legendSecondary: Secondary suppression: when exactly one gender cell is hidden while the total is published, the smallest remaining gender cell is hidden as well, so the first cannot be recovered by subtraction.
admin.kpi.legendSmallCells: Small-cell rule: every date × activity × gender combination with fewer than {k} people is dropped before storage, so the finest table the dashboard can reach never contains a small cell.
admin.kpi.legendGender: The gender columns come only from a voluntary self-report given at onboarding; whoever did not answer is counted as “not reported” and is never guessed or inferred.
admin.kpi.legendCounts: Under each value: the number of distinct people behind it (when the indicator is person-level) and the number of events it was computed from.
admin.run.gateExplainer: A computed run is a candidate, not a publication. Nothing appears on the dashboard until a person publishes a run here.
admin.run.computed: Run {id} was computed. It is not published yet.
admin.run.published: The run is published and the dashboard now shows it.
admin.run.rejected: The run is rejected. Nothing from it is published.
admin.run.noteRequired: A note is required when rejecting a run.
admin.run.emptyBody: Compute a run to see it here. Publishing it is a separate, human decision.
admin.run.caption: KPI runs and their review status
admin.run.checklist: Before publishing, check that every small cell is suppressed, that no gender cell can be recovered from the total, and that the definitions version is the one you are willing to quote.
admin.dash.title: Institution dashboard
admin.dash.lead: The published KPI run, the disclosure review behind it, the aggregated heat map, the internal quality metrics and the onboarding timing log.
admin.dash.provisionalTitle: The K01–K23 definitions are provisional placeholders
admin.dash.provisionalBody: They were not taken from SIP Draft §11 — that document was not available when this prototype was built. They must be replaced with the definitions of SIP Draft §11, and the run recomputed, before any figure on this screen is quoted, reported or presented.
admin.dash.provisionalVersion: Definition file in use: {version}. Every stored aggregate is flagged as computed from a provisional definition.
admin.dash.provisionalSource: What the definition file itself says
admin.dash.gateTitle: Nothing appears here until a run is published
admin.dash.gateBody: This dashboard reads one source only: the latest computed run that passed the disclosure review and was published. A freshly computed run stays invisible until a person publishes it in the review section below.
admin.dash.publishedStatus: Showing the published run computed on {when}.
admin.dash.noPublishedStatus: No run is published — the tables below are empty on purpose.
admin.dash.kpiLead: Computed from stored events only; no figure in this table was ever typed in by hand.
admin.dash.noPublishedBody: Compute a run in the disclosure review below and publish it. Until a run is published, this dashboard shows no figures at all.
admin.dash.definitionsUnavailable: The definition file could not be loaded; indicators are shown with the labels stored in the run.
admin.dash.reviewLead: Compute a candidate run, check what the suppression rules hid, then publish or reject it. Only a published run reaches the tables above.
admin.dash.heatLead: Aggregated cells of the published run, never an individual track.
admin.dash.qualityLead: Speech-to-text error rate, response cache and the monthly spend cap of the assistant.
admin.dash.timingLead: Active authoring time and elapsed time, in two separate columns.
admin.dash.scopeTitle: What these figures are, and what they are not
admin.dash.scopePrototype: This is a prototype built for an application, running on sample data and fictional accounts. It is not a production service, it has no real users, and no technology-readiness level is claimed for it.
admin.dash.scopeEvents: Every figure is computed from stored events by the KPI engine; no number on this screen was typed in by hand.
admin.dash.scopeGender: Gender figures come only from a voluntary self-report; people who did not answer are counted as “not reported” and are never inferred.
admin.dash.scopeSuppression: Any cell backed by fewer than {k} distinct people or devices is suppressed: it shows “suppressed (k<{k})” and never a number.
admin.dash.scopeDefinitions: The K01–K23 definitions are provisional until SIP Draft §11 is transcribed into the definition file; the engine reads that file, so replacing the definitions changes every figure without a code change.
admin.dash.scopeQuality: The speech-to-text error rate is measured on synthetic stand-in samples until consented recordings of elderly Montenegrin speakers replace them.
admin.heat.cellRule: Visits are aggregated on a grid of roughly 100 m. A cell exists only when at least {k} distinct pseudonymous devices are behind it; anything below the threshold is not drawn and not counted anywhere on this screen.
admin.heat.ariaLabel: Map of {count} aggregated visit cells on the Vrmac hill
admin.heat.emptyBody: Either no run is published, or no cell reached {k} distinct devices. Nothing below the threshold is drawn.
admin.heat.legendHidden: A cell with fewer than {k} distinct devices is not drawn, and its count appears nowhere else either.
admin.heat.legendAggregate: Each square is a count of visits inside that square, not a path: the map cannot be read back to a person or a device.
admin.heat.legendNoTracks: Only the centre of the cell and the counts are published; the dashboard never receives an individual position.
admin.quality.notKpi: Internal engineering metrics, not indicators of the programme. They are shown so the figures above can be judged.
admin.quality.sttSynthetic: Measured on synthetic stand-in samples. These are not recordings of real speakers: the figure describes the test harness, not accuracy in the field, and must be measured again on consented recordings of elderly Montenegrin speakers before it is quoted.
admin.quality.sttNone: No speech-to-text evaluation has been run yet.
admin.quality.sttHow: The word error rate is computed per sample against a reference transcript; the mean and the median of the latest evaluation run are shown.
admin.quality.budgetNotBillable: no billable provider is configured in this prototype
admin.quality.unavailable: The API did not report this.
admin.timing.targetRule: The {minutes}-minute target applies to ACTIVE authoring time only — the time counted from heartbeats while a host was actually working. Elapsed time includes every wait, review and interruption and is never compared with the target.
admin.timing.columnsRule: The two are kept in separate columns; they are never added together and never shown as one number.
admin.timing.caption: Onboarding sessions: active authoring time against the {minutes}-minute target, with elapsed time in separate columns
admin.timing.colActiveHelp: heartbeats only — this is what the target applies to
admin.timing.colElapsedHelp: wall clock — includes every wait, not compared with the target
admin.timing.emptyBody: No host has started a voice onboarding session yet, or the timing endpoint is not available.
admin.timing.footnote: Session identifiers are pseudonymous and the log carries durations only — never a name, a recording or a transcript.
